craft_claim: Non-Anglophone traditions independently develop light invented worlds and delight in their own invention, so whimsy is not an Anglophone-specific attitude.

supporting_evidence.location: Bengali nonsense collection, U. Ray and Sons, 19 September 1923
supporting_evidence.note: Ray's collection established literary nonsense in Bengali, inventing compound creatures and rule-governed absurd situations that delight in their own making.
Calvino builds fanciful stories from scientific premises in Italian, with an anthropomorphized narrator, demonstrating an independent Italian practice of light invention.
Jansson's first Moomin book, written in Swedish, builds a habitable invented world with whimsical creatures, a third independent tradition.

counterevidence.note: The traditions differ mechanically: Bengali nonsense foregrounds sound-play and portmanteau, the Italian practice foregrounds conceptual literalization, and the Finland-Swedish practice foregrounds world-building, so no single universal technique should be asserted.

scope: Cross-cultural scope of the tone; the basis for card section 8.
exceptions: Translation blurs each tradition's defining wordplay, so claims rest on documented traditions and scholarship rather than on any single English rendering.
